questions.question: The never-ending movement of water between the Earth and the sky is called the ___ cycle.
questions.funFact: The water you drink today may be the same water that dinosaurs drank millions of years ago!

questions.question: When water is heated and turns into vapour, this is called ___.
questions.funFact: The Sun heats up rivers and seas, turning some water into invisible vapour that rises into the sky.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of the air around us?
questions.funFact: About four out of every five parts of the air is nitrogen, and only about one part is the oxygen we breathe.

questions.question: Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius.
questions.funFact: Water is unusual because it grows bigger when it freezes, which is why ice floats on top of water.

questions.question: A rainbow has ___ colours.
questions.funFact: The seven rainbow colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a form of water?
questions.funFact: Water can be a solid (ice), a liquid (rain) or a gas (steam), but sand is none of these.

questions.question: Match each weather word to what it means.
questions.funFact: All kinds of weather happen in the lowest layer of air, close to the ground.

questions.question: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
questions.funFact: When these tiny water drops join together and become heavy, they fall down as rain.

questions.question: The gas that humans need to breathe from the air is ___.
questions.funFact: Trees and plants make the oxygen we breathe, which is one big reason they are so important.

questions.question: Moving air is called ___.
questions.funFact: Wind can be a gentle breeze or a powerful storm strong enough to move sailing boats.

questions.question: In India, the season of heavy rains from June to September is called the ___.
questions.funFact: Farmers across India wait eagerly for the monsoon rains to water their crops.

questions.question: Most of the Earth's surface is covered by water.
questions.funFact: About seven-tenths of the Earth is covered in water, which is why it looks blue from space.
